title: M1.5: Email inbound parsing and threading
description:
Pure email adapter functions: parse raw MIME (headers, text/plain, text/html converted to text, quoted-reply stripping with the original kept in S3, attachment extraction to S3 references), normalize addresses (case, plus tag split), derive the conversation key from References/In-Reply-To/Message-ID, and the plus-tag HMAC correlator as a lookup hint only. Cap body text at 100 KB with a reference to the raw object. Behavior is in Gherkin through the fake pipeline; parsers and normalizers are unit tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- A reply that quotes an earlier Message-ID lands in the same channel even when References is stripped
- A changed subject does not split a thread; an unknown reference starts a new channel
- HTML-only mail becomes readable text; tracking pixels and remote images are never fetched
- A plus-tagged address with a bad HMAC still routes by headers or starts a new thread; the tag never authorizes anything
- Non-UTF-8 charsets and malformed MIME do not crash the ingress; they produce a counted refusal

Gherkin: features/email_threading.feature and features/email_inbound_parsing.feature

Depends on: M1.3

Contract: the External channels contract (initiative description; draft docs/EXTERNAL_CHANNELS.draft.md).

Process: Gherkin first (AGENTS.md outside-in). Write the named feature, add it to features/cucumber-features.txt, implement steps in conversation/features-support/steps/, then production code. Vitest only for pure helpers. Both cucumber-js and vitest must pass. No emojis, no compatibility forks, tenant_id on every item, strangers get 404. Product PR into develop with sub-agent review.
